chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us (via him) who said: Ahmad ibn Mabindath narrated to us who said: Ahmad ibn Hilal narrated to us who said: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Qaysi narrated to us, from Abul Haytham al-Maythami, from Abu Abdullah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he said:
If three names succeed one another: Muhammad, Ali, and al-Hasan, then the fourth of them will be their Qa'im.

key_terms.تَوَالَتْ: Succeeded one another / followed in succession

ai.seo_question: Who is the fourth Imam referred to as Qa'im in the succession of Muhammad, Ali, and al-Hasan?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* establishes a prophetic chain of naming that links the first three Imams—Muhammad, Ali, and al-Hasan—to the fourth, Imam al-Mahdi, as the *Qa'im* who will rise. In Shia scholarship, this succession underscores the continuity of the Imamate and identifies al-Mahdi as the culmination of this specific lineage, reinforcing his status as the eschatological restorer of justice.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (26) Muhammad bin Hammam narrated from Ahmad bin Mabindath from Ahmad bin Hilal from Ahmad bin Ali al-Qayssi from Abul Haytham al-Maythami that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said: “
If three names (of the infallible imams); Muhammad, Ali and al-Hasan succeed, then the fourth will be al-Qa’im.”
